- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the forecast horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., sentiment < 0.3) — model fails to account for downward pressure.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +/–), model overreacts to recent sentiment shifts, causing lagged or delayed corrections.
- Model consistently overpredicts mid-to-late horizon (days 15–30) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — adjust downward by 1–2% for days 20+.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to cap price growth — apply a ceiling rule at +5% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >1.2) and price is rising, model tends to overfit recent trend — reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for horizon >10 days.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model often fails to reverse trend — apply a “sentiment reversal” rule: if sentiment drops below -0.5 for 2+ days, reduce forecast by 2–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
